items.title: Indra Jatra opens with ceremonial pole raised at Hanumandhoka
items.desc: The eight-day festival began with the traditional erection of the Indra flagpole, marking the start of celebrations honouring the god of rain and prosperity.

items.title: Guterres recalls Nepal glacier warning as climate risks grow
items.desc: The UN chief said the impacts of climate change are arriving sooner and hitting harder, calling for more adaptation finance and a stronger Loss and Damage Fund as Nepal seeks international support after the August floods.

items.title: Flood destroys equipment, pushing back Siddhababa tunnel opening
items.desc: Replacement electromechanical equipment must be brought through the Korala border, delaying the planned start of traffic by at least a month.

items.title: Khanal holds multiple diplomatic meetings in New York as Nepal establishes ties with Grenada
items.desc: The foreign minister discusses flood recovery, development cooperation and stronger economic ties with his Indian counterpart, US officials and other foreign ministers during the UN General Assembly sidelines.

items.title: US announces additional $31 million support for Nepal’s flood recovery
items.desc: The package includes funding for permanent bridges, humanitarian assistance and US-made drones, taking Washington’s total flood response and recovery support to more than $36 million.

items.desc: With eight karatekas, including star Arika Gurung and a kata team, eliminated in Nagoya, Sherpa remains Nepal’s sole hope to avoid a medal drought. He faces Macau’s On Tek Leong in the quarterfinal today.

items.title: World number 3 Chandra Bahadur loses his first bout
items.desc: He becomes the third Nepali boxer to fail to progress from the preliminaries. Four Nepali boxers are yet to face their opponents across different weight categories.

items.title: Nepal women’s kabaddi team edges Thailand, men’s team crashes out
items.desc: The women’s team rallied from nine down to beat Thailand 46-43 in Nagoya, while three group-stage losses ended the men’s medal hopes with a match still in hand.

items.title: Nepal, India agree to review treaty amid widening trade deficit
items.desc: Experts call for changes to non-tariff barriers, reciprocal duty-free provisions, trade facilitation and investment as Nepal’s exports remain heavily dependent on a few products.

items.title: Nepal’s rhino census is getting a scientific makeover
items.desc: Authorities are considering DNA sampling and camera traps to replace a decades-old method that relies on elephants and direct sightings.

items.title: For Bhotekoshi flood survivors, the tuin is an ordeal
items.desc: In Nuwakot, locals walk for five to six hours to reach the tuin, an improvised cable crossing, then wait for another four to five hours to cross.

items.desc: Shah will address the UN General Assembly on Thursday.

items.title: Child abuse allegations shake ISKCON’s Kathmandu centre
items.desc: The religious organisation’s global leadership has suspended eight Nepal-based officials pending an inquiry, nearly five months after a family reported alleged abuse to police. The person accused of sexually abusing a girl remains at large.

items.title: Amresh Kumar Singh warns of a disruption to Nepal’s geopolitical balance
items.desc: Singh says the government has failed to maintain balanced ties with Nepal’s neighbours, build private-sector confidence and deliver meaningful progress on good governance.

items.title: Supreme Court upholds Resham Chaudhary’s presidential pardon
items.desc: Court dismisses writ petition challenging the decision to waive the former lawmaker’s life sentence for the 2015 Tikapur killings.

items.title: Seven die of scrub typhus in one month in Salyan
items.desc: Health workers have begun door-to-door testing and treatment as two to five people test positive each day in the rural municipality.

items.desc: China regularly describes the issue of Taiwan, which Beijing views ‌as its own territory, as its most sensitive and important diplomatic issue and has repeatedly called for arms sales to stop.

items.title: Pedestrian overpass takes shape in Babarmahal
items.desc: The footbridge is being built along the busy Maitighar–New Baneshwar section to make road crossings safer for pedestrians.

items.title: Prime Minister Balendra Shah, Malaysian counterpart discuss ending middlemen in labour migration
items.desc: Nepal’s prime minister says syndicates and intermediaries have harmed workers and calls for direct talks between the two countries’ labour ministers.

items.title: Nepal-Japan festival to mark 70 years of diplomatic ties
items.desc: The November 22 event in Kathmandu will feature Japanese band Godiego, Nepali artists and cultural, tourism and commercial activities.

items.desc: The driver who died of burns was allegedly using driving licences issued in other people’s names.
